cards.explanation: The answer is that Abraham goes out to mourn and weep for her. Sarah dies in Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, and "…Abraham went out to mourn and to weep for her." (Genesis 23:2) The text gives us mourning and weeping, plain and simple. I think a man who loses his wife is allowed every one of those tears, friends.

The word is burial. Abraham says, "Give me a burial site among you so that I can bury my dead." (Genesis 23:4) He opens by calling himself a foreigner and an outsider among the Hittites. Then he makes his request, friends: a burial site.

The answer is True. The Hittites tell Abraham, "Bury your dead in the finest of our tombs. None of us will withhold his tomb for burying your dead." (Genesis 23:6) That's a generous answer to a man who just called himself an outsider. Nobody shuts a door on him, friends.

The answer is that he rises and bows down before them. "Then Abraham rose and bowed down before the people of the land, the Hittites." (Genesis 23:7) They had just called him God's chosen one, and he answers by bowing low. I think that's a man who doesn't let a compliment go to his head, bakers.

The answer is that Ephron gives the cave to Abraham as a gift. Ephron says, "I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it." (Genesis 23:11) He says it in front of his own people, with everyone at the city gate listening. That's a big offer said out loud, friends.

The answer is True. Ephron says he gives the field and the cave (Genesis 23:11), and Abraham answers, "…I will pay you the price of the field. Accept it from me, so that I may bury my dead there." (Genesis 23:13) He bows again before the people of the land and asks to pay. Gift offered, payment requested. That's quite a moment, bakers.

The word is full. Abraham first asks that Ephron sell it to him "…for full price…" (Genesis 23:9) Then he "…weighed out for him the price he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver…" (Genesis 23:16) No discount, no haggling down, friends.

The answer is False. The text says the field, the cave, "and all the trees within the boundaries of the field were deeded over to Abraham's possession" in front of the Hittites at the gate (Genesis 23:17-18). So the trees are part of the package, not left with Ephron. That's like buying the whole batch and getting every last crumb in the bag, friends. Then Abraham buries his wife Sarah in that cave (Genesis 23:19).

The answer is that he buries his wife Sarah in the cave. "After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre…" (Genesis 23:19) All that talking at the gate was about this one thing, friends. Now Sarah has her resting place.
